punchline: Atlassian's FedEx Day fixed only the clock: 24 hours, any topic, then show it.
thirty_sec: In 2005 Atlassian gave its developers a day to build anything outside their regular work, as long as they delivered something to show within 24 hours. The name comes from FedEx's overnight promise. Daniel Pink uses it in Drive as an example of autonomy, and the format was modeled on Google's 20 percent time. Companies running such days report new skills and collaborations, though there are no measured figures.
